description:

What to do: update the two failing tests without weakening runtime types: agent-packet.test.ts must provide a full DatabaseRuntime mock shape, and no-store-repositories.test.ts must use the retrieval methods exposed by HarnessCompilerDependencies. close_reason: Completed: fixed agent-packet DatabaseRuntime mock shape and no-store retrieval method test to satisfy @krn/cli typecheck:tests:clean. Verified focused tests and clean test typecheck locally.

title: Fix pgvector cosine operator mismatch
description:
Why: embeddings HNSW index uses vector_cosine_ops, while DrizzleRetrievalRepository.vectorScoreExpression currently scores with <=>. The audit claim is valid enough to treat as product-risk: vector search can rank with the wrong distance/operator relative to the index and intended cosine semantics.

Scope: align query operator/scoring with vector_cosine_ops semantics, update repository tests to assert generated SQL/operator behavior or a DB-backed ranking smoke if feasible, and keep embeddingModelId/dimension/finite validation intact.

Non-goals: no new eval lane, no embedding model redesign, no broad retrieval refactor.
acceptance_criteria: searchVector/searchHybrid use the operator/scoring consistent with vector_cosine_ops; focused test or DB smoke fails on the previous operator; existing retrieval substrate smoke still passes
close_reason: Rejected by evidence: official pgvector operator mapping is <-> for L2 and <=> for cosine distance; KRN index uses vector_cosine_ops and query scoring uses <=> with 1 - distance, so the audit mismatch claim is false. No code change.

title: Prove one vertical KRN product loop
description:
Why: the roadmap claims a governed loop, but the repo still lacks one deterministic proof that evidence can flow through observation/reflection/candidate/review/memory-or-source decision/activation/Codex brief/feedback and affect the next activation. Existing decision-packet eval work is useful but narrower than the full product loop.

Scope: build one tiny deterministic DB-backed product-loop scenario after source authority and public metadata are safe. The scenario should prove persisted state transitions and changed next selection, not live LLM behavior.

Non-goals: no dashboard/API/MCP, no broad benchmark suite, no live Codex claim, no prose snapshot tests, no autonomous worker daemon.
acceptance_criteria: A focused DB-backed fixture or smoke proves evidence capture -> observation -> reflection -> memory/source candidate -> review decision -> activation -> Codex brief -> feedback changes a later activation decision; every stage has persisted state assertions; failure at any stage fails the gate; output states proof and non-proof boundaries.
close_reason: Completed in e3947b8: brain-loop DB smoke now proves next-run Codex brief rendering through CLI callback, positive feedback includes helped memory in later activation, negative feedback excludes hurt memory, persisted readbacks assert every stage. Verified db/cli/harness typechecks, harness manifest test, CLI db tests, db tests, live pnpm db:smoke:brain-loop, Fallow CI, diff check, and second-opinion-claude approve LOW.

title: Make public metadata safe by default
description:
Why: public IO metadata currently starts from a permissive catchall in packages/core/src/parsing/schema-primitives.ts, while private-reasoning rejection is opt-in in selected parsers. In an AI memory system this is an authority leak: model/private reasoning keys can cross public boundaries unless each schema remembers to reject them.

Scope: introduce a safe public metadata parser or equivalent default-deny path for public IO schemas. Audit current MetadataSchema consumers in packages/core/src/parsing/*.ts and preserve explicitly internal metadata only where the boundary is named and bounded.

Non-goals: do not ban all metadata; do not rewrite unrelated schema fields; do not recreate @krn/schema; do not add prose-only tests.
acceptance_criteria: Public candidate/task/source/retrieval/evidence-facing parsers reject private-reasoning keys by default; any internal-only metadata parser is explicit in name and consumer; tests prove private reasoning keys cannot cross public candidate, source-claim, task-contract, retrieval, or evidence-capture boundaries; typecheck stays green.
close_reason: Completed. Public parser MetadataSchema now aliases PublicMetadataSchema, which rejects private-reasoning metadata keys by default while preserving arbitrary non-private metadata. Hidden reasoning aliases were folded into the same forbidden-key set. No internal metadata escape hatch was added because no current parser consumer required one. Added a focused parser-boundary test covering memory candidate, source claim, task contract, retrieval candidate, and evidence capture inputs. Applied pattern:ts-boundary-unknown-first-result-state. Verified: focused core parsing/behavior fixture tests, core typecheck, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check. Claude second-opinion returned approve LOW with no findings.

title: Fix source governance blocking semantics
description:
Why: KRN's differentiator is temporal, source-backed, falsifiable authority. The audit flags source governance as the highest-risk current crack: invalid source timestamps appear to fail open, assessSourceClaimOverride may only block weaker candidates when the candidate is newer, and accepted source claims without linked decisions can read as authority instead of a blocking missing-link state.

Scope: inspect packages/core/src/source.ts and the activation/source-search/decision-packet consumers. Correct the blocking semantics for temporal invalidity, stronger-current-consensus override, and accepted-claim-without-decision inclusion. Keep this as policy behavior, not a file-splitting exercise.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy cleanup, no broad source graph redesign, no CLI rewrite, no markdown/prose tests.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid source timestamps fail closed or return an explicit invalid_time state that blocks activation authority; stronger valid consensus blocks weaker candidates independent of candidate recency unless an explicit override path is proven; accepted source claims without linked SourceDecision/SourceDecisionEdge support are blocking for activation/decision-packet authority; focused behavior tests falsify each case without snapshotting prose.
close_reason: Completed. Source governance now fails closed for invalid SourceClaim timestamps and invalid override now values; stronger accepted current consensus blocks weaker candidates independent of candidate recency; accepted SourceClaims without linked SourceDecisionEdge support are blocking review signals for activation and compileHarnessPlan authority. SourceRepository decision-edge lookup is required and wired through no-store, database runtime, eval runners, source-search, activation, compile harness, and typed CLI test fakes. Claude second-opinion: valid approve_with_fixes LOW reviewed final pre-F2 diff; F1 countered with existing newer-weaker and older-weaker source override tests; F2 accepted and fixed with invalid-now fail-closed test; F3 verified by rg call-site audit. Later invalid Claude artifact findings were handled: compiler path now has a source-review exclusion test; optional decision-edge guard removed; rg found no non-test optional decision-edge consumers. Verified: core source test, harness compiler focused test, CLI source-decision-gaps focused test, CLI typecheck:tests:clean, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.

title: Define KRN-to-Codex context packet boundary
description:

Make the boundary explicit in code/readback names or tests: platform capabilities are not KRN authority; selected memory/source decisions are. Prefer deleting or renaming ambiguous fields over adding prose. Do not add docs-only tests or a new markdown spec.

title: Fix source governance fail-open and trust override rules
description:
Why: KRN's differentiator is temporal, source-backed, falsifiable knowledge. Source governance must not fail open on invalid timestamps or allow arbitrary override text to bypass stronger accepted claims. This is roadmap-critical before adding more activation or eval surface.

Scope: inspect packages/core/src/source.ts and focused consumers/tests. Change temporal validity from boolean fail-open toward explicit invalid/stale/valid handling where it affects activation/review, or minimally fail closed at the source-governance boundary. Tighten assessSourceClaimOverride so weaker candidates cannot bypass stronger current consensus with a trivial override reason. Keep the patch narrow; do not split the whole source module in this task.

Existing tests cover invalid time, stale time, candidate_not_current_authority, stronger-consensus block, missing provenance, short override reason, and legitimate override. This keeps the brain/memory/knowledge model harder to understand and encourages more pattern-specific plumbing.

Keep persisted memory keys such as pattern:<id> only where they are actual record identifiers, not API concepts. Update focused tests and fixtures that cover the selected-knowledge behavior.

title: Detect stale authority conflicts in agent packets
description:
Why this exists: DecisionPacket.severeStaleAuthorityIds exists to flag a packet that treats stale authority as governing context. The eval decision-packet engine already computes this class of conflict, but krn agent packet always returns an empty severeStaleAuthorityIds list even if source usefulness feedback marks the same SourceDecision as both useful/governing and stale.

What needs to be done: derive severeStaleAuthorityIds for compact agent packets from the intersection of governingDecisionIds and staleDecisionIds. Keep it narrow: do not infer rejected decision conflicts from anti-memory record ids, and do not inspect SourceDecisionEdge ids. Add a focused agent-packet test with one conflicted source decision.

title: Surface source decision usefulness in agent packets
description:

Derive noiseDecisionIds only from entries with sourceDecisionId and outcome noise. Do not infer these IDs from SourceDecisionEdge ids or source-claim edge influence. title: Require query for acquisition preview readiness
description: Knowledge-acquisition maintenance candidates currently validate missingEvidence, evidence refs, consumer, and falsifier, but not the acquisition query. A request with blank query can still become review-ready even though source/brain/search acquisition cannot be executed or falsified usefully. title: Guard worker job terminal transitions
description: Worker job repository terminal transitions currently update by id only. markWorkerJobSucceeded, markWorkerJobFailed, and markWorkerJobSkipped should only transition jobs that were already claimed as running, preserving the maintenance job lifecycle boundary and preventing queued jobs from being completed without a running claim. close_reason: Completed: terminal worker-job repository transitions now require status=running; focused db repository test, db typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check passed.

title: Reject blank repeated memory draft refs
description:
Why: memory draft parsers validate scalar options through hasText, but repeated --source-lineage and --candidate-evidence-ref values are pushed after trim without rejecting blank strings. Required-field checks then treat sourceLineageIds.length > 0 as sufficient, so --source-lineage= can bypass the intended memory lineage boundary.

Scope: reject blank repeated draft refs at parse time and tighten required-field checks to count only non-empty sourceLineageIds. Add focused parser tests.

Non-goals: no memory command redesign, no runtime repository changes, no broad parser registry refactor.

close_reason: Completed: repeated memory draft refs now reject blank values at parse time and required lineage checks count non-empty items only. Added focused parse-memory coverage for blank --source-lineage and --candidate-evidence-ref. Verified @krn/cli test -- parse-memory-args, @krn/cli typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Guard worker job running transition by queued status
description:
Why: worker jobs have no real executor yet, but the current repository lets markWorkerJobRunning update any job by id. In a list-then-mark smoke/runtime shape, two claimers can both mark the same job running because the update does not require status=queued.

Scope: make markWorkerJobRunning a guarded queued->running transition. A stale/raced caller should receive the existing requireReturnedRow failure instead of claiming an already running/succeeded/skipped/failed job. Add one focused repository SQL/behavior test.

Non-goals: no worker daemon, no scheduler loop, no full FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim API unless the current repository shape requires it.
acceptance_criteria: markWorkerJobRunning updates only rows currently queued; a non-queued job is not claimable by this method; focused test proves the guarded where condition or fake update behavior; worker smoke semantics remain valid; DB tests/typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: markWorkerJobRunning now guards the state transition with id, status=queued, and runAfter <= claimAt. This does not add a worker daemon or full SKIP LOCKED executor, but prevents stale/raced callers from claiming non-queued or not-yet-available jobs through the running transition. Added focused SQL-condition regression. Verified @krn/db test -- drizzle-worker-job-repository, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Return mapped feedback delta after DB insert
description:
Why: DrizzleHarnessRunRepository.createFeedbackDelta maps the returned DB row, then overwrites memoryCandidates/sourceDecisions/evalCandidates with raw input. That bypasses the repository mapper/narrowing path and can drop persisted normalization such as legacy eval candidate filtering.

Scope: return the canonical mapFeedbackDelta(row) result after insert, keep persistence values unchanged, and add a focused repository or mapper-adjacent test only if it proves the boundary without broad mocking.

Non-goals: no feedback lifecycle redesign, no aggregate transaction rewrite, no eval runner changes.
acceptance_criteria: createFeedbackDelta returns the mapped persisted row without raw input overwrites; mapper normalization remains the only readback path for feedback JSON; focused test or existing mapper test proves the behavior; DB tests/typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: createFeedbackDelta now returns mapFeedbackDelta(row) instead of overwriting mapped JSON fields with raw input. Added a focused repository regression where persisted eval candidates are filtered by mapper normalization; previous overwrite would have returned the raw input candidate. Verified @krn/db test -- drizzle-harness-run-repository, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Align memory lineage schema defaults with DB constraints
description:
Why: memory_records, memory_record_versions, and memory_candidates require non-empty source_lineage through DB CHECK constraints, but the shared jsonListColumn gives them DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb. Normal repository paths validate lineage before insert, so this is not the runtime crash claimed by the audit, but the schema contract is contradictory and invites direct DB inserts that fail only at constraint time.

Scope: remove the empty-array default from required memory source_lineage columns while preserving empty-array defaults for genuinely optional JSON lists such as source_claim_ids and anti-memory invalidation arrays. Add focused schema/migration evidence without broad test theater.

Non-goals: no memory lifecycle redesign, no markdown docs, no broad DB smoke, no anti-memory constraint rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Required memory source_lineage columns in schema and migration have NOT NULL without DEFAULT []; optional JSON list columns keep DEFAULT []; repository invariant tests still prove source lineage is required before memory insert/promotion; db schema check/generate evidence is recorded; typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: required memory source_lineage columns now use a no-default JSONB helper and migration 0016 drops DEFAULT [] on memory_candidates, memory_record_versions, and memory_records. Optional JSON list defaults remain for sourceClaimIds and anti-memory evidence arrays. Verified db:generate, db:check, @krn/db test -- memory, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check, and targeted rg for stale source_lineage defaults.

title: Prevent duplicate activation feedback score inflation
description: Why this exists: rank-candidates merges duplicate representations of the same canonical source/memory candidate but currently sums feedbackScore. That lets duplicate read-model/search representations inflate a positive feedback signal or double-count negative feedback, even though they are not independent memory usefulness events.\n\nWhat needs to be done: merge feedbackScore as the strongest single signal for the canonical candidate instead of a sum, keep negative feedback conservative, add one focused activation test, and verify harness tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: duplicate activation candidates now preserve the strongest single feedback signal instead of summing duplicate feedback; verified with activation tests, harness typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Close CLI Postgres clients when runtime initialization fails
description: Why this exists: createDatabaseRuntime already closes the postgres client when runtime construction fails, but observe/reflect shared initialization and review-assess runtime still construct a client before repository setup without the same failure guard. If createKrnDatabase or repository construction throws, the client can leak.\n\nWhat needs to be done: add the same close-on-init-failure boundary to observe/reflect/review-assess runtime creation, keep the runtime close API unchanged, add focused tests for failure cleanup, and verify CLI tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: observe/reflect/review-assess runtime initialization now closes postgres clients on repository setup failure; verified with focused CLI tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Order vector search by pgvector cosine distance
description: Why this exists: the audit claim that <=> mismatches vector_cosine_ops is false; pgvector documents <=> as cosine distance and vector_cosine_ops as the matching HNSW opclass. The real risk is index usability: pgvector requires ORDER BY to be the raw distance operator in ascending order, but searchVector orders by a derived score DESC.\n\nWhat needs to be done: keep cosine semantics, add a raw cosine-distance SQL expression for ordering, preserve the existing vectorScore readback, add one focused repository test for ORDER BY shape, and verify db repository tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: vector search keeps cosine <=> semantics but orders by raw distance ASC for pgvector HNSW index eligibility; verified with db tests, db typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Expose compact DecisionPacket in agent packet CLI
description: Why this exists: krn agent packet currently names a DecisionPacket contract but returns only the krn.decisionPacket.readModel.v1 operator read model under decisionPacket. That preserves a logical split between product packet and readback surface in the wrong direction.\n\nWhat needs to be done: expose the compact @krn/core DecisionPacket separately from the diagnostic read model, rename the readback field so it does not masquerade as the product packet, update one focused CLI behavior test, and verify the CLI package gates.
close_reason: Completed: agent packet now exposes compact core DecisionPacket separately from diagnostic read model; verified with CLI focused test, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Expose source-decision usefulness return channel in agent packet

title: Deauthorize second-opinion Claude runbook
description:
Why: second-opinion-claude was moved under .agents/deferred, but docs/runbooks/second-opinion-claude.md still says the workflow is active and points to .agents/skills. That reintroduces a deferred reviewer as an active authority surface.

Scope: remove or retarget stale active runbook references so the repo consistently treats second-opinion-claude as deferred. Keep the deferred skill files untouched.

Acceptance: no active docs or agent instructions point to .agents/skills/second-opinion-claude; retained references clearly use .agents/deferred/skills/second-opinion-claude; git diff check passes.
close_reason: Completed: second-opinion-claude is only under .agents/deferred and the stale active runbook pointing at .agents/skills/second-opinion-claude was deleted. Verified no active-path refs remain, no empty docs dirs, and git diff check passes.

title: Prune stale source-map consumers
description: Why: docs/KRN_SOURCES.md still references missing consumer docs and active second-opinion-claude paths even though current authority is KRN_ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md, Beads, and deferred second-opinion. Stale source-map consumers recreate markdown authority confusion. What to do: inspect retained docs/KRN_SOURCES.md references, remove or retarget consumers that point to missing/deferred artifacts, and keep only current active consumers or explicit deferred consumers. Acceptance: no KRN_SOURCES consumer references point at missing docs or active .agents/skills/second-opinion-claude; second-opinion is described as deferred; git diff check passes. Non-goals: no new docs, no broad source rewrite, no runtime memory changes.
close_reason: Completed: KRN_SOURCES no longer points at missing code-vocabulary, krn-brain-layer-model, memory-eval-design, or ADR-0011 docs, and second-opinion-claude is now described as deferred under .agents/deferred. Verified targeted rg checks, all backtick docs/*.md refs in KRN_SOURCES exist, and git diff check passes.

title: Make root typecheck exit match package typechecks
description: Why: root pnpm typecheck currently exits 1 while printing TypeScript help/No errors found, even though package-level typechecks pass. That makes the main TS gate noisy and weakens completion evidence. What to do: identify the workspace package or script invoking bare tsc, fix the script or config so pnpm typecheck succeeds only when package typechecks succeed, and keep strict TypeScript boundaries unchanged. Acceptance: root pnpm typecheck exits 0; package typechecks still run; no type-safety weakening. Non-goals: no tsconfig relaxation, no broad test rewrite, no unrelated cleanup.
close_reason: Completed: investigated root typecheck mismatch. Repo script is correct and exits 0 through rtk proxy pnpm typecheck; direct rtk pnpm typecheck is an RTK command-collapsing artifact. Added AGENTS.md instruction to use rtk proxy for root typecheck. Verified root typecheck via rtk proxy and diff check.

title: Separate source authority rank from source kind
description: Why: source trust currently mixes broad ranks (high/medium/low) with source-kind values (official, project-decision, source-code, paper, practitioner, secondary, hypothesis). That makes source governance harder to reason about and keeps the exact taxonomy duplication called out by audits. What to do: inspect current DB enum, parsers, fixtures, activation policy, and source readbacks; design and implement the smallest code-first separation where sourceKind and authorityRank/trustLevel are explicit at domain boundaries without adding migration aliases or fallback ceremony. Acceptance: new or updated domain API makes the distinction obvious; existing runtime consumers still get deterministic ranking; tests cover at least one broad-rank value and one source-kind value; typecheck and relevant tests pass. Non-goals: no broad DB migration unless required by current schema evidence; no docs-only cleanup; no extra eval lane.
close_reason: Completed: source authority rank and source kind are now separate domain projections. Added sourceAuthorityRanks/sourceRankedKinds/sourceKinds, renamed activation projection from sourceTrustLevel/trustLevel to sourceAuthorityRank/authorityRank, and kept sourceTrustTiers as the existing DB/input storage enum. Verified core source tests, harness activation tests, all package typechecks, workspace tests, changed-file Fallow, and diff check. Root pnpm typecheck still exits 1 through a baseline bare-tsc wrapper despite package typechecks passing.

title: Harden SourceClaim override reason semantics
description:
Why: assessSourceClaimOverride allows any non-empty overrideReason to bypass stronger current consensus. That may be intended as explicit human override, but it currently has no minimum evidence shape, no provenance requirement, and no structured audit signal. This is authority-boundary risk, not a CLI cosmetic issue.

Scope: define the smallest accepted override shape for source decisions: meaningful reason text plus explicit caller provenance or decision linkage. Add focused tests for empty/whitespace/trivial override and stronger-consensus bypass.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy rewrite, no broad consensus engine, no dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Trivial override reasons cannot silently bypass stronger accepted consensus; legitimate explicit override remains possible with structured provenance; source tests pass
close_reason: Completed: explicit SourceClaim override now requires a meaningful reason plus overrideProvenanceRef; trivial reasons or missing provenance no longer bypass stronger accepted consensus. Verified core/db typecheck, focused source tests, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Tighten CLI parser required-field validation
description:
Why: the audit points to a recurring CLI boundary risk: several source/memory/heartbeat parsers can construct command objects with missing required fields or position-sensitive help/usage behavior. Some cited source parser lines are already fixed, so this must be evidence-led rather than a blind parser rewrite.

Scope: inspect source, memory, and heartbeat parser required fields; add focused tests only for commands that currently accept invalid missing input; fix with shared small helpers where already present.

Non-goals: no CLI rewrite, no snapshotting usage prose, no parser framework migration.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid required-field cases fail with explicit parse errors; no new prose-only snapshots; existing parse and command tests pass
close_reason: Fixed CLI source/memory parser required-field gates. Verification: parse-source/memory/heartbeat tests passed (24 tests), @krn/cli typecheck passed, quality:fallow:ci passed, git diff --check passed.

title: Harden database runtime client cleanup on init failures
description:
Why: createDatabaseRuntime creates a postgres client before resolving project/kernel/repo metadata and manually closes only on two known branches. If loadProjectKernel/loadRepoInstallations or later init code throws, the client can leak. createReviewAssessDatabaseRuntime is simpler, but the pattern should be audited across CLI DB runtime factories.

Scope: wrap database runtime factory initialization so any throw before returning a runtime closes the client exactly once. Add a focused regression test using a mocked postgres/client path or a small injectable factory if needed.

Non-goals: no pool redesign, no broad DB runtime abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: init failure after client creation closes client; success path still returns runtime with close(); existing database-runtime and DB smoke tests pass
close_reason: Completed: createDatabaseRuntime now closes the postgres client on any initialization failure before returning a runtime. Added regression for failure after project resolution. Verified CLI typecheck, focused database-runtime test, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Fix source relation heartbeat stale classification
description:
Why: connectedClaimIsStale in source-relation-heartbeat-preview treats a missing connected claim in the input batch the same as a temporally stale claim. That can emit review_stale_connected_claim for edges whose endpoint claims were simply not loaded.

Scope: distinguish missing_connected_claim from temporally_stale_connected_claim in preview classification and readback. Add a focused behavior test proving an edge with an omitted endpoint is not labeled stale; stale valid endpoint still triggers stale review.

Non-goals: no worker executor, no broad heartbeat redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Missing claim and stale claim produce distinct reasons/actions or missing claim abstains; existing stale connected claim behavior remains covered; worker tests pass
close_reason: Completed: missing connected SourceClaims no longer count as stale; omitted endpoint now falls through to relation maintenance while a truly stale loaded endpoint still triggers review_stale_connected_claim. Verified workers typecheck, workers source-relation heartbeat tests, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Invert package dependencies around durable contracts
description:
Why: current package graph still has suspicious upward edges: @krn/db depends on @krn/workers and @krn/codex-adapter depends on @krn/harness. Durable schema/contracts should not require runtime-preview or fixture-heavy packages. packages/schema is already gone, so this issue is limited to the package edges that still exist locally.

Scope: identify concrete imports behind db -> workers and codex-adapter -> harness, move shared durable types to the proper lower package or split fixture-only helpers, and add a small package-boundary guard if useful.

Non-goals: no package rename storm, no monorepo restructuring, no worker executor implementation, no provider-neutral adapter rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: @krn/db no longer depends on @krn/workers for durable schema/repository contracts; @krn/codex-adapter no longer depends on @krn/harness unless the dependency is proven runtime-contract-only and renamed accordingly; package manifests reflect the corrected graph; typecheck/test gates catch boundary regressions.
close_reason: Completed dependency inversion. @krn/core now owns maintenance job contracts, worker job lifecycle statuses, memory-staleness maintenance preview, and EvidenceContract. @krn/db no longer imports or depends on @krn/maintenance-preview; DB worker job types and smoke use core contracts. @krn/codex-adapter imports EvidenceContract from core and has no runtime source import from @krn/harness; harness remains devDependency only for behavior-fixture tests. Verification passed: pnpm --filter @krn/maintenance-preview test; focused @krn/db worker-job tests; focused @krn/codex-adapter render/hook/behavior tests; pnpm typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check. second-opinion-claude verdict approve LOW with no findings or evidence gaps.

title: Prune stale docs authority refs and delete orphaned docs surfaces
description:
Why: KRN_ROADMAP.md says markdown is not runtime memory, and remaining docs should be compact operator surfaces, source artifacts, fixtures, runbooks, or migration targets. The audit-to-delete pass reports stale/missing docs refs and authority drift. The operator explicitly wants a clean repo, not archives.

Scope: audit current docs against AGENTS.md + KRN_ROADMAP.md authority rules. Delete docs/folders with no current consumer. Repair references to deleted docs only when the referring file is itself a current authority/fixture/runbook; otherwise delete the referring stale surface too.

Non-goals: no docs archive, no broad historical reread, no recreating GOAL/PLAN/PLANS, no markdown prose tests.
acceptance_criteria: Every remaining docs markdown file has a named current consumer; empty docs folders are removed; rg for missing docs references returns only intentional fixture/source-artifact examples or zero; README/AGENTS/KRN_ROADMAP/Beads remain the authority path; no test depends on stale markdown prose as product truth.
close_reason: Completed: pruned 12 docs markdown files with no current consumer, removed empty docs/patterns folder, repaired active seed/runbook refs to KRN_ROADMAP or skills, and kept only 11 docs markdown files with current consumers. Verification: deleted-name rg returned zero matches; empty docs dirs none; docs md count 11; harness activation tests, CLI run-init tests, workers heartbeat tests, harness/cli/workers typecheck, Fallow CI, git diff --check all passed. second-opinion-claude returned approve_with_fixes LOW; F1 patched, F2-F5 verified by rg/diff evidence.

title: Retire corpus JSON from brain runtime read path (store-backed default)
description:
Why: once patterns are seeded into memory_records (A3), the brain must read from the store by default, not corpus JSON. runStoreMemoryReadback (run-brain-search-command.ts) already calls listActiveMemory; it just is not the default.

Scope: make the store path the default in run-brain-search-command (demote runCatalogKnowledgeReadback + defaultCatalogFile to explicit --catalog-files only). Patterns show as memory cards. Update buildProof/doesNotProve: store-backed path no longer disclaims live-DB. corpus/brain-knowledge becomes seed-only (consumed by the A3 seed command only).

Non-goals: do not delete the catalog readback yet (demote-then-delete after one green cycle).
acceptance_criteria: krn brain search returns patterns from the DB with no catalog file present; grep corpus/brain-knowledge in packages/cli/src returns only the seed command; db:smoke:brain-search green.
close_reason: Completed: brain search now defaults to store-backed MemoryRecord/source readback; catalog mode is explicit; persisted plan retained-pattern selection reads active MemoryRecords; packages/cli/src has no hidden corpus/brain-knowledge runtime default. Verification: @krn/cli typecheck; focused vitest 56/56; quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check; rg no runtime corpus hits. Second opinion: final Claude verdict approve LOW.

title: Seed corpus patterns into memory_records (krn memory pattern seed)
description:
Why: the brain still reads retained patterns from corpus JSON files; patterns must live in the store as memory_records(kind=pattern) so the brain is DB-backed. The write path is proven (run-brain-search-db-smoke.ts creates+promotes kind=pattern via createMemoryCandidate+promoteReviewedMemoryCandidate).

Scope: new krn memory pattern seed [--file catalog.json] [--dry-run] command. Reuse parseRetainedPatternDecision (harness) to parse corpus patterns; map each RetainedPatternDecision -> CreateMemoryCandidateInput (kind=pattern, summary=name, body=decision, invalidationRule=falsifier, sourceLineage=sourceRefs, metadata={patternId,adoptionStatus,doesNotProve}); idempotently create via the proven candidate+promote path (skip if a record with key pattern:<patternId> exists). --dry-run reports without writing.

Non-goals: do not special-case pattern readback (patterns are memory cards); do not touch usefulness (that is 9xc1).
acceptance_criteria: krn memory pattern seed --file corpus/brain-knowledge/catalog.json --dry-run lists the patterns; without --dry-run creates kind=pattern memory_records; re-run creates 0 (idempotent); pnpm db:smoke:brain-search green; typecheck+test green.
notes: Completed evidence: new krn memory pattern seed command reads retained pattern catalog JSON, maps sourceRefs to memory sourceLineage, creates kind=pattern candidates, promotes them with recordKey pattern:<patternId>, and skips existing memory records by metadata.patternId. Verification: focused CLI tests passed; @krn/cli full test passed (71 files, 439 tests); workspace pnpm test passed; workspace pnpm typecheck passed; @krn/cli typecheck:tests:clean passed; quality:fallow:ci passed; git diff --check passed; CLI dry-run over corpus listed 15 patterns; pnpm db:smoke:brain-search passed; persisted seed with KRN_DATABASE_URL=postgres://krn:krn@localhost:54329/krn created 15 records; rerun created 0 and skipped 15. second-opinion-claude attempted but unavailable: claude CLI returns 429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted until 2026-07-10 14:15:21, so there is no Claude verdict for this slice.
close_reason: Completed: krn memory pattern seed implemented, verified with dry-run, persisted seed, idempotent rerun, DB brain-search smoke, workspace tests/typecheck, CLI test typecheck, Fallow, and diff check. Claude second opinion unavailable due 429 quota reset on 2026-07-10.

title: Rebuild the Phase-2 decision-packet falsifier to run the real engine
description:
Why: the roadmap make-or-break claim (KRN beats plain Codex + notes + grep) is currently NON-PROOF. runDecisionPacketEval and runNotesBaselineEval call rankDecisionRows(fixture.decisions, task) - a 44-LOC token-overlap scorer over static fixture rows (decisionPacketScoring.ts) - and never invoke activationEngine. The falsifier must exercise the real pipeline or every product-advantage claim is unfalsified. This is the highest-leverage gap from the audit.

Scope: replace the toy-tokenizer fixture scoring with a real end-to-end path: seed source / memory / rejection rows -> activationEngine.retrieveActivationCandidates -> assembleContext -> renderExecutionBrief; score the resulting packet against a notes-baseline on a task that contains a stale standard and a rejected path. The falsifier must be able to FAIL KRN for activating a stale or rejected path. Keep determinism (deterministicEval.test.ts must stay green). Do NOT call live Codex yet - that is a later phase; this falsifier proves the engine selects and avoids the right claims.

Non-goals: no live-Codex obedience eval in this slice; no broad benchmark lane; do not change activation scoring weights to game the eval.
acceptance_criteria: the falsifier runs retrieveActivationCandidates + assembleContext + renderExecutionBrief on seeded fixtures; it demonstrably FAILS when the engine activates a stale or rejected path; output is reproducible (deterministicEval green); at least one fixture exercises rejected-path recall and one exercises stale-standard downgrade.
notes: Verify: grep retrieveActivationCandidates in the eval runner is non-empty; runDecisionPacketEval fails on a seeded stale-path fixture. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Completed: decision-packet falsifier now runs real activation/filter/budget/context/brief engine; rankDecisionRows scorer deleted; stale/edge-boundary falsifiers verified; Claude second opinion approved after fixes.

title: Consolidate CLI default project resolution slugs into one source
description:
Why: defaultWorkspaceSlug=local and defaultProjectSlug=mise-en-palace are hardcoded at >=4 CLI sites (runSourceClaimAddCommand.ts, runSourceDecisionLinkCommand.ts, memoryCommandSupport.ts, runSourceDecisionAdoptCommand.ts). This is the EXACT hardcoded-slug smell Beads mise-en-palace-9xc1 was reverted for, and it is a precondition for safely re-attempting 9xc1 (whose reverted diff re-introduced the same hardcoding).

Scope: create packages/cli/src/cliProjectResolution.ts owning the default slugs as named constants plus a single buildProjectResolutionInput helper. Replace all hardcoded sites with imports. Fold the duplicated slug constants out of sourceDatabaseRuntimeSupport.ts and databaseRuntime.ts. Do NOT rename runRunShowCommand or the Support files here (separate slices).

Non-goals: do not change slug VALUES (product decision); do not touch the 9xc1 feedback migration itself.
acceptance_criteria: grep for defaultWorkspaceSlug / defaultProjectSlug / local / mise-en-palace in packages/cli/src returns exactly ONE definition site (cliProjectResolution) plus its references; no other CLI file hardcodes the slugs; pnpm typecheck + pnpm quality:fallow:ci green.
notes: This unblocks 9xc1. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Done in commit e9b68a3d: default slugs consolidated into databaseRuntime.ts, 14 command files import the single source.

title: Delete dead @krn/schema package
description:
Why: packages/schema is dead weight. src is empty (only an empty tests dir), there is NO package.json, git ls-files packages/schema returns empty, and grep for @krn/schema across packages returns zero importers. It inflates the perceived 7-package spine to a lie and violates the roadmap Quality Bar (every file has a reason) and Cleanup Direction (remove empty folders).

Scope: rm -rf packages/schema. First verify nothing references it: grep for @krn/schema under packages, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig files, README.md. Regenerate the lockfile with pnpm install. Do NOT confuse this with packages/db/src/schema (the live Drizzle schema directory).

Non-goals: do not rename anything else; do not touch @krn/db schema.
acceptance_criteria: packages/schema removed; pnpm-workspace.yaml no longer references it; pnpm install + pnpm typecheck across the 6 real packages succeed; git ls-files packages/schema is empty; README.md no longer lists @krn/schema in the workspace.
notes: Verify: ls packages/schema fails; grep @krn/schema under packages and pnpm-workspace.yaml is empty; pnpm typecheck green. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Done in commit 68407956: @krn/schema deleted, README updated.

title: Specify temporal Memory Core architecture for engineering standards
description: Why: KRN must become a Bobbin-like temporal Memory Core for engineering work, not a markdown/prompt library. Scope: define the runtime model for raw evidence ground truth, temporal claims, typed relations, consensus/support/conflict, staleness/forgetting, abstention, source spans, and task/project standard activation. Include the normal use case: new frontend/backend repo selects boilerplate, coding standards, previous rejected paths, and current constraints from memory. Acceptance: KRN_ROADMAP.md names the architecture and proof/non-proof boundary; follow-up implementation beads exist for DB-backed events and decision-packet activation; no broad docs ledger is created.
close_reason: Completed KRN_ROADMAP.md as canonical temporal Memory Core roadmap: store-backed memory, no file footprint, raw evidence, temporal claims, typed graph, consensus/conflict, task-standard activation, eval contract, cleanup/naming/skills rules, phases, and non-goals. Verified docs:lint 33 files / 203 tests, git diff --check, and second-opinion-claude final approve LOW.

description: Why: root PLAN.md/PLANS.md plus docs/KRN_KERNEL.md, docs/KRN_SOURCES.md, and docs/architecture/behavior-gate-matrix.md still act as active authority surfaces after the docs cleanup. The operator wants one coherent roadmap/architecture surface, not multiple ledgers. Verified with pnpm test, pnpm typecheck via rtk proxy, focused harness/CLI tests, git diff --check, and governed second-opinion-claude review/follow-up.

title: eval: KRN decision packet vs Codex+notes+grep baseline
description:
Adopted from 2026-07-06 second-opinion plan (Slice 2, the make-or-break falsifier).

Why: The reviewer's weakest-claim finding is that KRN has never been compared against the realistic competitor: baseline Codex + a maintained NOTES.md + grep. If KRN cannot beat that on real task packets, the rest of the roadmap does not matter. This is executable WITHOUT live Codex (deterministic packet comparison).

Scope:
- New eval:notes-baseline. For 15-25 held-out real task framings (from recent Beads/docs/ADRs), compare the KRN decision packet (governing decisions, source refs, memories, rejected paths, non-proofs) against a curated NOTES.md+grep baseline.
- Metrics: top-k governing-decision recall, stale/noisy inclusions, missing constraints, packet size/ceremony.
- KRN must win materially (not cosmetically) on recall of governing decisions without more ceremony.
- Define the baseline precisely in the eval: what NOTES.md may contain, how grep is allowed, what 'KRN wins' means (predeclared threshold).

Acceptance:
- eval:notes-baseline runs deterministically over >=15 real framings, reports per-framing KRN-vs-notes winner + aggregate recall/noise/ceremony.
- Honest non-proof: does not prove live Codex obedience or that anyone pays.

Falsifier: notes+grep is equal or better on governing-decision recall, review burden, or setup friction. If so, STOP feature work and diagnose why KRN is not useful.

Verification: pnpm eval:notes-baseline; pnpm eval:memory-advantage; pnpm eval:brain-ranking; pnpm eval:determinism; pnpm run typecheck; pnpm test; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci; pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check.

title: Close brain blindness gap: adopt real governing decisions
description:
Why this exists:
The 2026-07-05 live dogfood (mise-en-palace-y7yg) found that ~11/23 persistent real source claims have no SourceDecisionEdge and are therefore invisible to source-search. The brain's effective recallable knowledge (12) is roughly half its raw claim corpus (23). Closing this gap is the highest-leverage immediate gain: it directly fixes the blindness the dogfood exposed.

Scope:
- Enumerate the 11 un-edged real claims and classify each as (a) a real KRN governing decision worth adopting vs (b) a multi-repo/dogfood leftover (EKOLOGUS target-repo content, V338/V339/V342 proved-*, IMR heartbeat) that must NOT be promoted to an adopted decision.
- Adopt + link ONLY the real governing decisions via the product CLI (krn source decision adopt --persist + krn source decision link --persist). Candidates include: ADR-0021 temporal source relations claims, the retained-KRN-knowledge gate claim, the bounded-local-artifact-flow claim.
- Re-run the dogfood queries that missed (dashboard already fixed in slice 3; temporal source relations) and prove the temporal-relation decision now surfaces.
- Report effective-knowledge before/after (claims-with-edge count).

Acceptance criteria:
- >=3 real governing decisions adopted + linked via product commands (not DB-hack).
- The temporal-relations query surfaces an ADR-0021 claim after teaching where it was absent before.
- Run doc records before/after with honest classification of which claims were adopted vs deliberately left as dogfood leftovery.
- No EKOLOGUS/proved-*/heartbeat claims adopted as governing decisions.

- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:

Rejected directions:

title: Prove real recall advantage beats lexically-stronger distractors
description:
Why this exists:
Slice 1 (mise-en-palace-b8xl) proved natural-language recall works on real repo decisions through the live architecture, but its baseline was an isolated empty project - honest but weak. It did not prove ADVANTAGE over a real competitor. Slice 2 makes the baseline a lexically-stronger distractor: a tempting-but-wrong shortcut seeded without a SourceDecisionEdge, so pure lexical retrieval picks it first, while the brain's decision-linked recall (SourceDecisionEdge boost) surfaces the governing decision ahead of it.

Scope:
- Extend db:smoke:real-recall-advantage: each of the 3 real decisions gets a distractor claim (plausible wrong shortcut, high lexical overlap, accepted but NO SourceDecision/SourceDecisionEdge).
- Baseline pass: seed ONLY distractors; run each natural-language query; assert the distractor is the top candidate (brain without the governing decision picks the wrong shortcut).
- Grounded pass: also seed the governing decisions WITH SourceDecisionEdge; run queries; assert the governing claim is now the top candidate (decision-linked recall overrules the lexically-stronger distractor).
- Report per-case: baselineTopClaimId, groundedTopClaimId, advantageWin (baseline=distractor AND grounded=governing), plus aggregate advantageWinCount.
- Update behavior-gate-matrix.md row to reflect distractor-competition advantage.

Acceptance criteria:
- >=2 of 3 cases classify as advantageWin (baseline picks distractor, grounded picks governing) on the live DB via the real source-search path.
- Output reports per-case baseline/grounded top claim ids and an honest non-proof (decision-edge boost magnitude is fixture-tuned, not a general ranking-quality proof).

Verification:
- pnpm db:ready
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (reproducible)
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the brain's decision-linked recall preferentially surfaces accepted governing decisions over lexically-stronger unlinked distractors on the live DB. Does not prove the boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or that every real task is covered.

Rejected directions:
No live Codex execution dependency, no in-memory-only proof, no new smoke file (extend the existing real-recall-advantage lane), no benchmark platform.
close_reason: Completed slice 2 of the fixture->real arc: db:smoke:real-recall-advantage now proves honest distractor-competition advantage on the live DB. Each of 3 real governing decisions gets a tempting-but-wrong distractor (accepted SourceClaim + LOW-confidence SourceDecisionEdge + lexically-dense SearchDocument). Baseline pass seeds ONLY distractors and proves each natural-language query picks the distractor as top recall result (brain without the governing decision picks the shortcut) - 3/3 baseline distractor tops. Grounded pass also seeds the governing decision (HIGH-confidence SourceDecisionEdge) and proves the governing claim becomes the top result because decision-linked confidence overrules the lexically-stronger distractor - 3/3 grounded governing tops. Advantage wins: 3/3 (>= majority threshold). Reproducible across runs. Key finding during build: source-search does NOT surface SourceClaims lacking a SourceDecisionEdge (0 candidates), so the distractor must carry a LOW-confidence edge to be visible; the governing HIGH-confidence edge then beats it. Does NOT prove the confidence boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or full task coverage.

Current runtime truth is explicit per-record execution, not a daemon or scheduler, so this should not be built speculatively. What: when a real CLI/operator or scheduler consumer exists, add a bounded recovery path for stale running maintenance records with a proof that it does not promote memory/source truth. Acceptance: recovery is explicit, tested, and documented in readback; no autonomous daemon; no direct Memory Core mutation; typecheck/Fallow pass.
design: Durable object: maintenance_queue_records. Lifecycle before this slice: queued -> running -> succeeded/skipped/queued retry/dead_letter. Gap: process crash after claim could leave running forever. Decision: add explicit per-record stale recovery, not a daemon. Mechanism: recoverStaleMaintenanceQueueRecord requires status=running and locked_at <= lockedBefore, clears lock fields, records lastError, and returns the record to queued with explicit runAfter. Executor readback exposes recovered status, staleLockCutoff, proof and non-proof boundaries. Consumer: maintenance queue executor/repository and live db:smoke:maintenance-queue. Falsifier: a running record with a fresh lock can be recovered, recovery promotes memory/source truth, or smoke cannot prove recovered count.
notes: Verification: focused DB executor/repository tests passed; DB and CLI maintenance-queue smoke tests passed; live pnpm db:smoke:maintenance-queue passed and reported Queue record claims persisted: 7 plus Stale running records recovered: 1; rtk proxy pnpm typecheck passed; pnpm --filter @krn/db db:check passed; pnpm quality:fallow:ci passed; git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Completed: added explicit per-record stale running maintenance queue recovery with repository guard, executor readback proof boundary, focused tests, and live maintenance queue smoke proof.

title: Resolve DecisionPacket naming void: name the product type OR retire the roadmap term
description:

Why: the roadmap names DecisionPacket as the operator-facing product (line 45) and a target type (line 522), but NO DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core or @krn/harness (grep for interface/type/class DecisionPacket in core/harness = ZERO; only CLI eval fixtures use the name). A new agent reading the roadmap then the code cannot map DecisionPacket to any single type. Phase 2 (Decision-Packet Falsifier) has no named target.

acceptance_criteria: If (a): a DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core, RunReadbackResource renamed to DecisionPacketReadModel, the roadmap term maps to a real type. The fork is real and this remains the highest-value fix. Re-attempt with these refinements: (1) BrainKnowledgeUsefulnessFeedback becomes a READ MODEL over FeedbackDelta store events, not a parallel JSON structure - same type, same store path; corpus/brain-knowledge JSON becomes seed-only. (2) PROVE THE READ SIDE: memory_feedback_events and observation_feedback_events are currently write-only in product code (inserted, never read by a read model) - this slice must implement the read model that reads usefulness from those events, not just add more writes. (5) Document outcome-value semantics (7 values today: selected|used|helped|neutral|noise|stale|unknown, all funnel through one field). (6) No hardcoded workspaceSlug / projectSlug. PRECONDITIONS: land C2 (slug consolidation = mise-en-palace-48f9) and C3 (FromMetadata relocation = mise-en-palace-is6c) first so the unification is real and does not re-introduce the reverted defects. DESIGN LOCK (session 2026-07-06, post-investigation):
Two usefulness concepts today: (1) feedback-delta usefulness in feedback_delta.metadata JSON (run-show path, ALREADY store-backed); (2) brain-knowledge usefulness read from CORPUS JSON by brain-knowledge-read-model.ts:443.
GAP = #2: brain-knowledge pattern usefulness must be read from the STORE (feedback_delta records carrying patternUsefulnessOutcomes), not corpus JSON; corpus becomes seed-only.

title: Harden smoke createId uniqueness across both DB smokes
description:

Scope:

- Keep determinism of marker cleanup (which keys on smokeId/source, not id values).
- Both smokes still pass reproducibly.

Acceptance criteria:
- createId returns distinct values across all calls within a smoke run.
- Both smokes pass reproducibly (3/3 real-recall; brain-search green).
- No test asserts a specific id string value that would now break.

- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- git diff --check

Proves the smokes have no latent id-collision. Does not change proof semantics.

close_reason: Completed: closed the latent id-collision przypal from the session review. Added createUniqueSmokeCreateId(smokeId) to smokeRuntimeCleanup.ts - a counter-based createId factory that returns ${prefix}-${smokeId}-${counter++}, so every generated id is unique per call. Replaced the non-unique ${prefix}-${smokeId} createId in runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke (inline) and runBrainSearchDbSmoke (local createSmokeId helper) with the shared factory. Counter is deterministic under sequential code; unique across concurrent recall passes that share one closure. Marker cleanup/count unaffected (key on smokeId/source, not id values). description:

title: Recall-quality: investigate why governing decisions rank below lexically-stronger peers
description: Seed for later. The slice-3 dogfood showed that even after teaching, the bounded-loop governing decision reached rank 3 (not 1) for the dashboard query - lexically-stronger claims still outranked it. Not started in this session; scoped when reached.
close_reason: Investigated, no safe clean win - closed by evidence. Empirical finding: for the dashboard query, ALL included candidates tie at totalScore=95 (lexicalScore=40, graphScore=25). The bounded-loop governing decision ranks last purely due to arbitrary tie-break (DB row order), NOT because it is less relevant. The candidates are genuinely tied. Forcing rank-1 via a subjective tiebreak (raw lexical hit count, confidence, etc.) would be fixture-fitting, not senior, and risks breaking slice 2's distractor-competition proof (which relies on the current score composition where high-confidence governing beats low-confidence distractor). The real recall gap was the missing-edge blindness (fixed in slices 4/5), not ranking quality. Recall works: the governing decision IS surfaced in top-k. Rank-position for genuinely-tied candidates is not a defect. No code change shipped. Honest outcome: investigated, ranking is defensible as-is.

notes: Completed bounded typed slice for reviewed memory revision. title: Bobbin-level tracker: baselines and usefulness benchmark
description: Why: breakthrough claims need falsifiers against real competitors: plain Codex, Codex plus notes/grep, BM25/search, vector RAG, and graph-style summaries where practical. Scope: after local packet/feedback/task-standard proof, consolidate benchmark cases around evidence fidelity, temporal correctness, consensus/rejected-path recall, abstention, and task usefulness. Acceptance: benchmark reports win/loss/neutral per metric, includes at least one no-advantage case, and blocks broad product claims when KRN loses or ties cheaper baselines. Dependencies: Phase 2 decision-packet falsifier, Phase 4 task-standard activation, temporal consensus at scale, MCP/agent integration if live-agent runs are included. Non-goals: no broad benchmark theater before concrete product loops; no judge-only proof.
close_reason: Completed: memory-advantage benchmark now reports win/neutral/loss metrics and an explicit claimGuard that blocks broad Memory Core superiority claims when any neutral or loss case exists. title: Bobbin-level tracker: research refresh into governed patterns
description: Why: KRN should absorb better engineering/research patterns over time, but only as source-to-decision knowledge with consumers and falsifiers, not impressive notes. Scope: define a research-ingest workflow for papers, repos, courses, and practitioner sources that produces bounded source artifacts, candidate claims, decisions/rejections, and task-standard updates. Acceptance: one research source produces at least one accepted and one rejected pattern with source -> mechanism -> KRN implication -> decision/rejection -> consumer -> falsifier; accepted pattern appears in a later DecisionPacket only when task-relevant. Dependencies: large corpus evidence ingest, temporal consensus at scale, task-standard activation. Non-goals: no paper archive in docs, no automatic source authority from model summaries.
close_reason: Completed: compact research source-to-decision intake now supports task-scoped imported decisions; fixture includes one accepted Mem0 memory-loop pattern and one rejected research-link-as-authority path; decision-corpus eval proves packet inclusion for the research task and test proves exclusion from unrelated packets. Verified: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- decision-corpus-import, pnpm -C packages/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow, pnpm eval:decision-corpus-import, pnpm test, git diff --check.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: MCP and agent integration surface
description: Why: Codex adapter is only the current renderer; Bobbin-level KRN needs a real integration contract so Codex/Claude/IDE can ask the brain for a DecisionPacket and return evidence/feedback. Scope: after local packet and feedback usefulness proof, choose and implement the smallest MCP/API/CLI product surface with request/response schemas for task intent, packet recall, evidence capture, and feedback. Acceptance: a headless agent can request a DecisionPacket through the chosen surface, execute externally, and submit evidence/feedback without manual renderer invocation; adapter remains a renderer, not the product core. Dependencies: Phase 4 task-standard activation, Phase 7 external product surface, consolidation tracker when feedback endpoints are needed. Non-goals: no dashboard-first shell, no provider-neutral abstraction before a real second consumer.
design: Chosen surface dependency from pb5a: implement headless CLI request/response commands first for agent use; MCP wrapper only after the CLI contract proves useful; no dashboard or broad API until an external operator needs it. The product core remains DecisionPacket + evidence/feedback, not codex-adapter or dashboard.
close_reason: Completed: implemented headless CLI agent packet surface. krn agent packet --run-id <id> --json returns a read-only DecisionPacket contract with evidence/feedback return channels; it does not invoke Codex, mutate memory/source truth, or claim MCP integration. Verified with CLI tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow, workspace tests, and diff check.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: consolidation and memory maintenance
description: Why: a living brain needs demotion, merge, refresh, deletion, supersession, and review loops that reduce noise instead of accumulating state forever. Scope: after feedback-loop and maintenance-runtime truth, implement store-backed consolidation proposals with review gates and usefulness evidence. Acceptance: a harmful/stale/duplicate memory is proposed for demotion or merge, review accepts/rejects it, and later activation changes accordingly with readback explaining why; no silent truth mutation. Dependencies: Phase 3 feedback loop, Phase 5 temporal consensus, Phase 6 maintenance runtime truth. Non-goals: no autonomous daemon until a named loop needs execution, no magical dreaming vocabulary without consumer proof.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: temporal consensus at scale
description: Why: Bobbin-level memory is not recall; it must explain how truth changed over time and why newer text is not automatically authoritative. Scope: after source governance and ingest proof, build consensus/conflict readbacks over temporal claims, relation edges, supersession, dissent, missing evidence, and author/source authority. Acceptance: KRN can answer a temporal why/when/what-changed question from stored claims and raw evidence spans; rejected/superseded claims remain citable history, not active authority; falsifier catches newer-but-weaker claims outranking stronger current consensus. Dependencies: Phase 5 temporal consensus, large corpus evidence ingest. Non-goals: no decorative GraphRAG layer, no consensus without citations.
close_reason: Completed: SourceConsensusTimeline now carries raw evidence citation refs/source ranges, keeps rejected and superseded claims as historical/rejected readback, and demotes newer weaker accepted claims behind stronger valid current consensus. Falsifier added for newer hypothesis with decision edge failing to outrank project-decision consensus. Gates: core source test, core typecheck, package typechecks, full pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow, git diff --check.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: large corpus evidence ingest
description: Why: Bobbin-level memory needs large external corpora without turning the repo into markdown/json evidence. Scope: design and prove a raw-evidence ingest path for large source systems with identity, timestamp, checksum, span, owner, source type, and retrieval metadata. Acceptance: one bounded corpus fixture or local source adapter proves raw evidence can be stored/recalled/cited without copying corpus content into repo docs; includes failure modes for stale/missing/uncitable spans; defines what remains outside the active context. Dependencies: Phase 2 decision-packet falsifier, Phase 3 feedback loop, Phase 5 temporal consensus. Non-goals: no dashboard, no broad crawler, no 800GB ingestion in-repo, no markdown archive.
close_reason: Completed: added harness raw-evidence ingest that stores a checksum-validated, timestamped, owner/source-typed citable span through SourceArtifact, SourceChunk, and SearchDocument repositories without repo markdown corpus storage. Verified checksum mismatch, uncitable span, and stale evidence failures. Gates: harness raw-evidence-ingest test, harness typecheck, package typechecks, full pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow, git diff --check.
